_comment: Hand-authored field hints for the setup UI, layered over each manifest's own descriptions. Everything here was learned by configuring a real connector against a real tenant; when a hint names a trap, we hit it.

global.no_quotes: Enter values exactly as issued. Do not wrap them in quotes; the file format takes everything after the = sign verbatim, so quotes become part of the value and break authentication.

THREATLOCKER_BASE_URL.label: ThreatLocker instance

derive.input_help: The letter shown at your portal login, e.g. 'ThreatLocker Access (F)' means f. The wrong instance rejects your key in a way that looks like a bad key.

THREATLOCKER_BASE_URL.help: Only the instance letter is yours; the rest of the address is fixed.

THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID.label: Organization GUID
THREATLOCKER_ORG_ID.help: The GUID of your own organization, sent as the ManagedOrganizationId header. Most data calls refuse without it. Visible in the portal URL as organizationId=<guid> when viewing your organization.

THREATLOCKER_API_KEY.label: API key
THREATLOCKER_API_KEY.help: Create under Integrations > API Interface in the portal, on the SAME instance as the host above. Keys can carry an expiry date.

AUVIK_BASE_URL.label: Auvik region

derive.input_help: The code in your Auvik dashboard URL: if you sign in at us6.my.auvik.com, enter us6. Auvik's docs show auvikapi.us1... and tell you to swap the region; this does the swap for you.

AUVIK_BASE_URL.help: Only the region code is yours; the rest of the address is the same for everyone.

AUVIK_USERNAME.label: Auvik login email
AUVIK_USERNAME.help: The email of the Auvik user the API key belongs to. Sent with the key as a pair.

AUVIK_API_KEY.label: API key
AUVIK_API_KEY.help: Generate from your user profile in the Auvik portal.

derive.input_help: The address you open Hudu at in the browser, nothing after the host. The required /api/v1 is added for you; forgetting it by hand makes every call 404 while the connection looks healthy.

HUDU_API_KEY.label: API key
HUDU_API_KEY.help: Hudu portal: Admin > API Keys. A key scoped without password access is safest; the connector works fully except reading asset passwords.

derive.input_help: The address you open CIPP at in the browser. The required /api is added for you; without it every call reaches the CIPP web page instead of the API and looks like success.

CIPP_CLIENT_ID.label: API client ID
CIPP_CLIENT_ID.help: CIPP > Integrations > CIPP-API > Create New Client. A read-only Custom Role is the safe starting point. With the secret and tenant ID, the connector mints and refreshes its own tokens.

CIPP_TENANT_ID.label: Entra tenant ID
CIPP_TENANT_ID.help: The Microsoft Entra directory (tenant) ID hosting the CIPP API app registration.

HALOPSA_CLIENT_ID.label: API application client ID
HALOPSA_CLIENT_ID.help: From your Halo API application (Configuration > Integrations > HaloPSA API).

HALOPSA_TENANT.label: Tenant name
HALOPSA_TENANT.help: The 'yourmsp' in yourmsp.halopsa.com. Shown in your Halo URL and under Configuration > Advanced Settings.

HALOPSA_DOMAIN.label: Portal domain

derive.override_label: Using a custom domain instead of halopsa.com? Enter it

HALOPSA_DOMAIN.help: Derived from your tenant name automatically. Only fill the custom-domain box if your Halo lives on your own domain.

HALOPSA_OAUTH_SCOPE.label: OAuth scope
HALOPSA_OAUTH_SCOPE.help: Leave blank: defaults to "all", which matches most Halo API applications. Set only if yours is restricted to a narrower scope.

NINJAONE_CLIENT_ID.label: API app client ID
NINJAONE_CLIENT_ID.help: NinjaOne: Administration > Apps > API > Add. Choose the machine-to-machine (client credentials) type.

NINJAONE_OAUTH_SCOPE.label: OAuth scope
NINJAONE_OAUTH_SCOPE.help: Space-separated, and every word must be a scope the app actually has enabled, or the token request fails with invalid_scope. If unsure, enable only Monitoring on the app and enter: monitoring. That is also the right least-privilege posture for reads and reporting.

QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID.label: App client ID
QUICKBOOKS_CLIENT_ID.help: developer.intuit.com > your app > Keys & Credentials. Use the PRODUCTION keys for a real company file.

QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN.label: Refresh token (seed)
QUICKBOOKS_REFRESH_TOKEN.help: Easiest source: Intuit's OAuth 2.0 Playground. IMPORTANT: select YOUR app in the dropdown (not the sample app) with the com.intuit.quickbooks.accounting scope, authorize your company, and copy the refresh token. Intuit rotates this value; the connector persists rotations automatically, so this is only the seed.

QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID.label: Company (realm) ID
QUICKBOOKS_REALM_ID.help: Shown beside the refresh token in the OAuth Playground, and in any QuickBooks URL as companyid=<number>.

QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT.label: Environment
QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT.help: production for a real company, sandbox for an Intuit sandbox company. Must match where the refresh token was authorized.

IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN.label: Instance subdomain
IMMYBOT_SUBDOMAIN.help: The 'acme' in acme.immy.bot. Also derives the OAuth scope, so without it token requests are rejected.

IMMYBOT_TENANT_ID.label: Entra tenant ID
IMMYBOT_TENANT_ID.help: Directory ID of the Entra tenant your ImmyBot trusts.

IMMYBOT_CLIENT_ID.label: App registration client ID
IMMYBOT_CLIENT_ID.help: Register an app in Entra, then in ImmyBot: Show More > People > New > paste the Enterprise App object ID into 'AD External ID'.

HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN.label: Private App token
HUBSPOT_ACCESS_TOKEN.help: app.hubspot.com/private-apps > Create. Grant read scopes only (crm.objects.*.read, crm.lists.read, crm.schemas.*.read); the connector then physically cannot write regardless of what any agent asks.

HUNTRESS_API_KEY.label: API key
HUNTRESS_API_KEY.help: Huntress portal: top-right menu > API Credentials. Issued as a key + secret pair.

DATTO_BCDR_PUBLIC_KEY.label: Public key
DATTO_BCDR_PUBLIC_KEY.help: Datto partner portal: Admin > Integrations > API. Issued as a public/secret pair.

SHERWEB_CLIENT_ID.label: API client ID
SHERWEB_CLIENT_ID.help: From Sherweb's developer portal (api.sherweb.com): register an application.

SHERWEB_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY.label: Subscription key
SHERWEB_SUBSCRIPTION_KEY.help: The API-gateway subscription key from the same developer portal; sent alongside the OAuth token on every call.

CORK_API_KEY.label: API key
CORK_API_KEY.help: From the Cork portal's API settings.

AVANAN_APP_ID.label: SmartAPI App ID
AVANAN_APP_ID.help: Legacy Avanan portal: Security Settings > SmartAPI > create an API key. Issued as an App ID + Client Secret pair.

AVANAN_BASE_URL.label: Region API host
AVANAN_BASE_URL.help: Leave blank for US region 1 (the default). Credentials are region-locked, so if you are on another region use its smart-api host.
